title: Injectivity and kernel image of the ideal homology cycle map
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $I$ an ideal, $M$ an $R$-module and $P$ a projective resolution of $M$ with free terms [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Put $C=P\otimes_R R/I$. Let $\mu:I\otimes_R M\to M$ be $R$-linear with $\mu(a\otimes x)=ax$. Suppose $\delta_H:H_1(C)\to I\otimes_R M$ is $R$-linear and satisfies the following formula: for every cycle $z$, lift $y\in P_1$ with $z=y\otimes1$ and every finite expression $d_1y=\sum_j a_jp_j$, its value on $[z]$ is $\sum_j a_j\otimes\epsilon(p_j)$. Then $\delta_H$ is injective and its image is $\ker\mu$. This statement assumes the formula, not the existence of such a map.

source.place: Parent ideal-kernel naturality node, Steps 1–3; Stacks Algebra, proof of Tag 00M5 and Remark 00M6 (https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00M6).

proof.text: Represent each quotient cycle by y tensor 1 as in the finite tensor expansion. Its differential lies in I P_0 and therefore has a finite expression sum a_j p_j. The formula and epsilon d = 0 give mu delta_H = 0.

source.place: Parent ideal-kernel naturality node, Steps 1–3; Stacks Algebra, proof of Tag 00M5 and Remark 00M6 (https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00M6).

proof.text: For t in ker mu, lift t to I tensor P_0 using right exactness and the surjective augmentation. Its multiplication image in P_0 is killed by epsilon, hence equals d y by resolution exactness in degree zero. The element y tensor 1 is a quotient cycle and the formula sends its class to t. This proves the image equality.

source.place: Parent ideal-kernel naturality node, Steps 1–3; Stacks Algebra, proof of Tag 00M5 and Remark 00M6 (https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00M6).

proof.text: If the formula gives zero for a cycle class, right exactness for I tensor P identifies its ideal-tensor lift as a differential from I tensor P_1. Subtract its multiplication image from y. The result is an actual cycle in P_1, hence a boundary by exactness of the resolution in degree one. Reduction modulo I shows the original quotient cycle is a boundary. Since delta_H is linear, this proves injectivity.

theorem tor_ideal_homology_exactness
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R) (M : ModuleCat.{u} R)
    (P : ProjectiveResolution M) (hP : ∀ n : ℕ, Module.Free R (P.complex.X n))
    (μR : (I ⊗[R] M) →ₗ[R] M)
    (hμR : ∀ (a : I) (x : M), μR (a ⊗ₜ[R] x) = (a : R) • x)
    (δH : ((((tensoringRight (ModuleCat.{u} R)).obj (ModuleCat.of R (R ⧸ I))).mapHomologicalComplex
        (ComplexShape.down ℕ)).obj P.complex).homology 1 →ₗ[R] (I ⊗[R] M))
    (hδH : ∀ (z : ((((tensoringRight (ModuleCat.{u} R)).obj (ModuleCat.of R (R ⧸
        I))).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.down ℕ)).obj P.complex).cycles 1)
        (y : P.complex.X 1) (k : ℕ) (a : Fin k → I) (p : Fin k → P.complex.X 0),
        ((((tensoringRight (ModuleCat.{u} R)).obj (ModuleCat.of R (R ⧸ I))).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.down ℕ)).obj P.complex).iCycles 1 z = y ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : R ⧸ I) →
        P.complex.d 1 0 y = ∑ j, (a j : R) • p j →
        δH
          (((((tensoringRight (ModuleCat.{u} R)).obj (ModuleCat.of R (R ⧸ I))).mapHomologicalComplex
        (ComplexShape.down ℕ)).obj P.complex).homologyπ 1 z) =
          ∑ j, a j ⊗ₜ[R] P.π.f 0 (p j)) :
    Function.Injective δH ∧ LinearMap.range δH = LinearMap.ker μR
